findings.suggested_fix: On mount, set filled from the current input value in both the empty and nonempty cases, with a regression test that swaps controls under one Field.Root.
findings.title: Clear filled state when an empty control mounts
findings.why_it_matters: If a filled control is unmounted while its Field.Root remains mounted, mounting a new controlled control with an empty value leaves the field marked filled. The mount effect only sets filled for a nonempty DOM value, and useValueChanged skips the initial value, so the old state persists; synchronize both true and false on mount.

findings.title: Prevented controlled changes still clear errors and validate
findings.why_it_matters: A controlled field whose change event is prevented can still lose server errors and run validation when its onValueChange callback updates the value. The event handler returns before checking either native default prevention or details.cancel(), and the subsequent prop-change effect unconditionally clears errors and validates. This regresses the existing prevention behavior and also bypasses the newly supported cancellation signal.

findings.title: Sanitized controlled input values diverge from field state
findings.why_it_matters: When a controlled number or date input receives a programmatic value that the browser sanitizes to an empty string, the field reports filled and validates the unsanitized prop even though the displayed input and submitted form value are empty. The prop-change effect uses String(value) while form values are read from the DOM, so validators and field presentation disagree with the actual control. Synchronizing from the committed DOM value keeps both paths consistent.
